title: Tavo Walks in Silence
summary: Tavo is the quietest elephant in the herd, so quiet that nobody hears him coming. Until the day they need someone who makes no noise at all.

scenes.text:
On the savannah lived a very noisy herd of elephants.

When they walked, the ground shook with their stomping. When they said hello, they trumpeted so loudly that the birds flew out of the trees. When they bathed, the water splashed all the way up to the clouds.

All except Tavo.

Tavo was small and pale blue, and he walked so softly, so very softly, that nobody heard him coming.

At the waterhole, the others would sit on him by mistake.

"Oops, Tavo! I didn't see you."

In games, they forgot to count him.

"Tavo? Where was Tavo?"

He was there. He was always there. He just didn't make any noise.

One day, Tavo decided he'd had enough.

"Today I'm going to make some noise," he said. "Lots of noise."

He planted himself in the middle of the herd, lifted his trunk up high, filled his tummy with air… and trumpeted.

Out came a pfff.

A teeny-tiny pfff, like a balloon slowly going down.

The other elephants didn't even turn round.

Tavo lowered his trunk. And he went and sat on his own, in the shade of an acacia tree, without making a sound. As usual.

That afternoon, there came a very quiet crying.

It was a baby gazelle. She had wandered into some thorny bushes, and her legs had got all tangled up.

The big elephants rushed to help. But they arrived with such a racket, trumpeting so loudly, that the gazelle got even more frightened.

She kicked and kicked, and got even more tangled in the branches.

"Everybody stop!" said Grandma Elephant. "We'll hurt her like this."

Nobody knew what to do. If they went closer, the gazelle got scared. If they didn't go closer, they couldn't help her.

Then Tavo got up from the shade.

Tavo walked towards the bushes. Slowly. So slowly and so softly that the gazelle didn't even hear him coming.

By the time she saw him, he was already beside her.

"Shhh," Tavo said, in a whisper. "It's all right. I'm here now."

The gazelle stared at him with wide eyes. But Tavo didn't make any noise, and he wasn't scary. So she kept still.

With the tip of his trunk, branch by branch, Tavo set her free. Without a single tug. Without a single snap.

Until the gazelle was loose, and ran off to her mum, who was waiting at the edge of the savannah.

That night, Grandma Elephant came over to Tavo.

"Today we needed someone who could be quiet," she said. "And the only one who knew how was you."

Ever since that day, the elephants never forget to count Tavo.

And when one of the little ones in the herd is scared at night, or can't get to sleep, they all ask for the same thing:

"Can Tavo come?"

Tavo comes without a sound. He lies down beside them. And his silence is so soft and so warm that it's like a blanket.

After a little while, across the whole savannah, all you can hear is breathing.
